sheets.title: What setup asks a household first — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: This is the change in one picture. On main, "Set up your own" opens on connectors, step 1 of 4, and the first thing a family password installation is asked for is a connector directory endpoint and an environment key — a capability it will never use, in a ceremony it cannot skip past without skipping the rest. On this branch the first and only tab is capabilities, and it asks which kind of installation this is. The other four tabs are not hidden: they are contributions their capabilities register, so a device that has approved none has one tab, not five with four greyed out. `verify:static` now holds exactly this — "setup opens on the capabilities tab, and a device that approved nothing has no other" and "no directory endpoint is asked for before external connectors are chosen".

sheets.title: The same first screen on a phone — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: Two roads in, each a choice object and so allowed to carry words (DESIGN.md): core only, or choose. Nothing is applied by reading this screen — the ceremony ends on a review, and the review ends on Apply. On main the same width opens on the directory-endpoint form.

sheets.title: Choosing a purpose, then each capability — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: "Customize this installation" → five purposes, then one card per catalog capability with the 7 core ones first and always on. Family offers 12 optional capabilities of the 24 and pre-selects 4; Homelab and Custom offer all 24; Organization requires 2. Each card names what the capability does, what it adds, what it depends on, what leaves the device, and whether this distribution even contains it — read from the descriptor, so opening a card imports nothing and connects to nothing. The before is the same connectors form as the sheet above: this road does not exist on main at all, and the capture is honest about that rather than staging a comparison.

sheets.title: Settings › Capabilities, and the rail beside it — 1280 × 900
sheets.caption: Left: what an installation that has approved nothing carries. Seven core listings and Settings — no connections, access, identity, wallet or activity, and no drops or passkeys listing either. On main the same guest has 17 rail rows. Right: the new Settings tab, one row per catalog capability with its lifecycle, and on each optional row this device may have and is not running, an Add key. That key is new in this commit: until it landed a capability could be chosen once, in the setup ceremony, which lives before sign-in — so a person who signed in and then wanted drops had no road back. Adding goes through the same review and the same consent receipt as retiring. Note also that Connections has left the settings nav: it is the connectors capability's own category, not a core one.
sheets.before: 17 rail rows · nav: General Security Vaults Connections Danger
sheets.after: 9 rail rows · nav: General Security Vaults Capabilities Danger

sheets.title: The same list on a phone — 390 × 844
sheets.caption: 31 rows, 62px each, the same on both widths: the panel is a read-only list with one action per row, not a form. Status is a glyph and a short label, never a pill. On main this tab does not exist, so the before is the settings screen the same journey lands on — General — which is the screen a person actually sees there.
